prose: The author, who wrote a hackintosh guide a decade ago, says AI has revived the community. After Apple moved to ARM and macOS 27 dropped x86, he used a spare ThinkPad on macOS 26 and built an iOS app in a day with Xcode's Claude Code and Codex integrations, without writing code. He says hackintosh and 'hackios' activity has exploded in recent weeks thanks to AI-assisted reverse engineering, and lists projects like macOS 27 on a Snapdragon laptop, macOS 27.2 beta on an RK3588 board and iOS 17 on a Switch OLED.
highlights: macOS 27 dropped x86, but AI tooling revived the hackintosh scene
Claude Code with Ghidra credited for reverse engineering gains
Examples: Snapdragon laptop, RK3588 board, Switch OLED
Author built an iOS app in a day with AI help
